objects.description: Enumeration in namespace igl selecting the weighting scheme used when computing per-vertex normals for a triangle mesh. Values indicate how incident face normals contribute to each vertex normal: uniform, area-weighted, angle-weighted, a default (area) choice, and a count of the available types. Intended for use with the per_vertex_normals function templates in this header.

functions.name: igl::avg_edge_length
functions.description: Computes the average edge length of a mesh specified by vertex positions V and face indices F. Intended for triangle meshes; documentation notes faces must be simplices (e.g., triangles). Typical usage is to pass V as an #V-by-dim Eigen matrix of vertex coordinates and F as an #F-by-simplex_size Eigen matrix of indices into V; the function returns a scalar average of all edge lengths across the mesh elements.
requirements: V must be an Eigen matrix type derived from Eigen::MatrixBase (e.g., Eigen::MatrixXd) with size #V-by-dim (dim ≥ 2 as implied by geometry processing use).
F must be an Eigen matrix type derived from Eigen::MatrixBase (e.g., Eigen::MatrixXi) with size #F-by-simplex_size and must represent simplices (documentation: “must be simplex”; commonly triangles).
All indices in F must be valid indices into the rows of V (inferred from mesh conventions).
V and F must describe a consistent mesh (same indexing convention; inferred).
Behavior for non-simplex faces or invalid indices is unspecified; callers should ensure inputs satisfy the above to avoid undefined behavior (inferred).

functions.name: igl::barycenter
functions.description: Computes the barycenter (arithmetic mean of corner vertex positions) of each simplex defined by F over the vertex set V. V contains vertex coordinates (#V x dim). F contains indices of simplex corners into V (#F x simplex_size). The output BC is resized to (#F x dim) and filled with the barycenter of each corresponding simplex row in F. Typical usage: for triangle meshes (F has 3 columns), compute face centroids; for tetrahedral meshes (4 columns), compute cell centroids. Details such as exact scalar types are templated over Eigen types.
requirements: V must be a dense Eigen matrix or compatible Eigen expression with shape (#V x dim) holding coordinate values; its scalar type should be numeric (e.g., float or double).
F must be a dense Eigen matrix or compatible Eigen expression with shape (#F x simplex_size) holding indices into the rows of V; its scalar type should be an integral type.
All entries of F must be valid indices in the range [0, #V-1] and must reference existing rows of V.
Each row of F must define a simplex of consistent size (e.g., 2 for segments, 3 for triangles, 4 for tetrahedra); barycenters are computed as the mean of the referenced vertex positions per row.
BC must be an Eigen PlainObject (e.g., Matrix) that is writable and resizable; it will be resized to (#F x dim) by the function.
V and F must have compatible dimensions: the indices in each row of F must reference vertices in V, and the output dimension of BC equals the column count of V.
Input matrices should be properly initialized; uninitialized or NaN/Inf values in V will propagate to BC.

functions.name: igl::per_vertex_normals
functions.description: Compute per-vertex normals for a triangle mesh from vertex positions V and triangle indices F, using the specified weighting scheme. The result N contains one 3D normal per vertex. Typical usage: call with V (#V x 3), F (#F x 3) and choose a weighting type (e.g., UNIFORM, AREA, ANGLE, DEFAULT). The function accumulates incident face normals at each vertex according to the weighting, then produces per-vertex normals.
requirements: V must be a #V x 3 matrix of 3D vertex positions (floating-point scalars implied by normals).
F must be a #F x 3 matrix of triangle vertex indices (integral type indices).
F’s indices must be in the range [0, V.rows()-1].
weighting must be a valid igl::PerVertexNormalsWeightingType value (UNIFORM, AREA, ANGLE, or DEFAULT).
N is an output parameter (#V x 3) and will be written/reshaped by the function; pass a writable PlainObjectBase.
Inputs must represent a valid (triangular) mesh; behavior is undefined otherwise.
All inputs must be compatible Eigen types (DerivedV/DerivedF/DerivedN must satisfy Eigen::MatrixBase/PlainObjectBase requirements).

functions.name: igl::readOBJ
functions.signature:
template <typename Scalar, typename Index>
IGL_INLINE bool igl::readOBJ(
  const std::string obj_file_name,
  std::vector<std::vector<Scalar> >& V,
  std::vector<std::vector<Scalar> >& TC,
  std::vector<std::vector<Scalar> >& N,
  std::vector<std::vector<Index> >& F,
  std::vector<std::vector<Index> >& FTC,
  std::vector<std::vector<Index> >& FN,
  std::vector<std::tuple<std::string, Index, Index> >& FM
);
functions.description: Reads an ASCII Wavefront OBJ file from a filesystem path and parses mesh data into vector-of-vector containers: vertex positions (V), texture coordinates (TC), normals (N), and per-face index lists for positions (F), texcoords (FTC), and normals (FN). Also fills FM with per-face metadata tuples. Returns true on successful parse, false on error. Notes: The code comment suggests FM may conceptually include material and indices, but the declared tuple type is std::tuple<std::string, Index, Index>; exact FM semantics are not fully documented here.
requirements: obj_file_name must reference a readable .obj file path.
V, TC, N, F, FTC, FN, and FM must be valid lvalue references; contents will be overwritten/filled by the function.
Scalar is the numeric type for vertex-related arrays; values are read as double and cast to Scalar.
Index is the integral type for index arrays; values are read as int and cast to Index.
Faces may be of arbitrary degree (non-triangular faces are allowed).
Return value must be checked by the caller; false indicates a read/parse failure.

functions.name: igl::writeOBJ
functions.description: Writes a triangular/quad mesh with optional normals and texture coordinates to an ASCII .obj file. Use when you have vertex positions (V), face indices (F), per-normal vectors (CN) with their corner indices (FN), and texture coordinates (TC) with their corner indices (FTC). Returns true on success, false on error. Note: the parameter order differs from readOBJ as noted in the header.
requirements: str must be a valid path to a writable output file.
V must be a #V x 3 matrix of vertex positions (3D).
F must be a #F x 3 or #F x 4 matrix of indices referencing rows of V.
CN must be a #CN x 3 matrix of normal vectors if provided.
FN must be a #F x 3 or #F x 4 matrix of corner normal indices referencing rows of CN if CN/FN are provided.
TC must be a #TC x 2 or #TC x 3 matrix of texture coordinates if provided.
FTC must be a #F x 3 or #F x 4 matrix of corner texture coordinate indices referencing rows of TC if TC/FTC are provided.
All indices in F, FN, and FTC must be valid (in-range) indices into V, CN, and TC respectively.
Matrix arguments must be Eigen types compatible with Eigen::MatrixBase.
Caller should check the boolean return value to detect I/O or formatting errors.

data_types.description: An unconstrained byte buffer produced by the fuzzer. It may contain any sequence of bytes and is interpreted by the stub as a generic entropy source to derive numbers, indices, or coordinates. No specific encoding, structure, or character set is assumed.

A text file following the Wavefront .obj format, potentially accompanied by material references. Contains lines such as v (vertex positions), vt (texture coordinates), vn (normals), and f (faces that reference indices). Faces may be polygons (3+ vertices) and indices may include separate position/texcoord/normal fields with optional slashes. Whitespace, comments (#), and varying index bases may appear.

A string interpreted as a filesystem path to a file to be created or written by the target function. It may include directories and filename components; no constraints on content beyond being a valid path for the runtime environment.

import random
import struct
import math

# This generator aims to feed FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME with valid, interesting mesh data
# suitable for igl::barycenter and igl::per_vertex_normals stubs. The stubs consume the
# buffer as an entropy source to derive sizes, coordinates, and indices. We thus encode
# a compact mesh description with:
# - Header controlling dimension, simplex size, counts
# - Vertex coordinates in ranges expected by the stub mapping
# - Face indices in-range
# We produce one coherent byte stream under 4096 bytes.

# Helper: pack unsigned 32-bit
_def_u32 = lambda x: struct.pack('>I', x & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def _rand_vec(rng, n, a=-1000.0, b=1000.0):
    return [rng.uniform(a, b) for _ in range(n)]


def _tri_soup_grid(rng, nx, ny):
    # Produce a simple triangle grid (nx by ny quads split into tris) on z=0 plane
    # Returns (V, F) with V 3D and F triangles
    V = []
    for j in range(ny + 1):
        for i in range(nx + 1):
            # jitter to avoid degeneracy but keep reasonable scale
            x = i + rng.uniform(-0.05, 0.05)
            y = j + rng.uniform(-0.05, 0.05)
            z = rng.uniform(-0.02, 0.02)
            V.extend([x, y, z])
    def vid(i, j):
        return j * (nx + 1) + i
    F = []
    for j in range(ny):
        for i in range(nx):
            v00 = vid(i, j)
            v10 = vid(i + 1, j)
            v01 = vid(i, j + 1)
            v11 = vid(i + 1, j + 1)
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                F.extend([v00, v10, v11])
                F.extend([v00, v11, v01])
            else:
                F.extend([v00, v10, v01])
                F.extend([v10, v11, v01])
    return V, F


def _random_tri_mesh(rng, nv, nf):
    # Make a random but valid triangle mesh soup by sampling points on a sphere and
    # connecting random triples; guarantees indices in-range, though may be non-manifold.
    V = []
    for _ in range(nv):
        # Sample on/near unit sphere with small noise for variety
        th = rng.uniform(0, 2 * math.pi)
        ph = math.acos(rng.uniform(-1, 1))
        r = 1.0 + rng.uniform(-0.1, 0.1)
        x = r * math.sin(ph) * math.cos(th)
        y = r * math.sin(ph) * math.sin(th)
        z = r * math.cos(ph)
        V.extend([x, y, z])
    F = []
    for _ in range(nf):
        a = rng.randrange(nv)
        b = rng.randrange(nv)
        c = rng.randrange(nv)
        # ensure not all equal; minor attempt to avoid degenerate triangles
        if a == b == c:
            b = (b + 1) % nv
        F.extend([a, b, c])
    return V, F


def _pack_mesh_to_bytes(rng, V, F, dim=3):
    # The stubs read bytes into u32 streams. We'll pack sizes then raw floats/ints.
    # Layout:
    # [magic 4B] [dim 1B] [simplex_size 1B] [reserved 2B]
    # [nV u32] [nF u32]
    # V: nV * dim doubles (big endian IEEE754)
    # F: nF * simplex_size u32 indices
    # Keep under 4096 bytes.
    simplex_size = 3
    nV = len(V) // dim
    nF = len(F) // simplex_size
    header = bytearray()
    header += b'IGLB'  # magic
    header += bytes([dim & 0xFF])
    header += bytes([simplex_size & 0xFF])
    header += b'\x00\x00'
    header += _def_u32(nV)
    header += _def_u32(nF)
    body = bytearray()
    # pack V as doubles so the stub's u32 assembly still yields well-distributed bits
    for i in range(nV):
        for c in range(dim):
            body += struct.pack('>d', float(V[dim * i + c]))
    # pack F as u32
    for i in range(nF):
        for c in range(simplex_size):
            body += _def_u32(int(F[simplex_size * i + c]))
    data = bytes(header + body)
    # If too large, downscale by decimating faces
    if len(data) > 4096:
        # reduce faces to fit
        max_faces_bytes = 4096 - len(header) - (nV * dim * 8)
        if max_faces_bytes < 12:
            # fall back to only vertices
            nF = 0
            data = bytes(header[:8] + _def_u32(nV) + _def_u32(0) + body[: nV * dim * 8])
        else:
            max_faces = max_faces_bytes // (3 * 4)
            nF2 = max(1, min(nF, max_faces))
            body_v = body[: nV * dim * 8]
            body_f = bytearray()
            step = max(1, nF // nF2)
            count = 0
            for i in range(0, nF, step):
                if count >= nF2:
                    break
                a = F[3 * i: 3 * i + 3]
                for v in a:
                    body_f += _def_u32(int(v))
                count += 1
            data = bytes(header[:8] + _def_u32(nV) + _def_u32(count) + body_v + body_f)
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Decide between a structured grid mesh and a random spherical soup to vary normals
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.5:
        nx = rng.randint(2, 12)
        ny = rng.randint(2, 12)
        V, F = _tri_soup_grid(rng, nx, ny)
    else:
        nv = rng.randint(8, 200)
        nf = rng.randint(12, 400)
        V, F = _random_tri_mesh(rng, nv, nf)
    # Ensure counts are reasonable and indices in-range
    dim = 3
    nV = len(V) // dim
    simplex = 3
    # Clamp faces indices to range just in case
    F_clamped = []
    for i in range(0, len(F), 3):
        a, b, c = F[i], F[i + 1], F[i + 2]
        F_clamped.extend([int(a) % nV, int(b) % nV, int(c) % nV])
    data = _pack_mesh_to_bytes(rng, V, F_clamped, dim=dim)
    # Prepend a small variety prefix to influence stub's u32 extraction paths
    # Include varying bytes that change modulo decisions inside stubs
    prefix = bytearray()
    # Two u32 values for nv/nf selection paths in per_vertex_normals stub
    prefix += _def_u32(rng.getrandbits(32))
    prefix += _def_u32(rng.getrandbits(32))
    # Add a few random bytes
    prefix += bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 16)))
    out = bytes(prefix) + data
    return out[:4096]

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces a plausible writable filesystem path string.
# The target fuzzer stub calls FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() to obtain a path
# where it will write an OBJ file. We therefore generate a path that is:
# - Short (well under 4096 bytes)
# - Likely writable in typical sandboxed environments (use relative paths)
# - Sometimes includes subdirectories (the harness may create them)
# - With common filename patterns and extensions (.obj), plus variations
# - ASCII with occasional unicode-safe characters
# The returned bytes are the UTF-8 encoding of the path string.

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"

UNICODE_FRAGMENTS = [
    "Δmesh", "模型", "сет", "maillage", "网格", "mezcla", "mesh", "normal", "uv",
    "face", "顶点", "knoten", "tri", "quad", "顶点法线", "テスト", "테스트"
]

EXTS = [".obj", ".OBJ", ".Obj"]

DIR_NAMES = [
    "out", "tmp", "work", "test", "fuzz", "obj", "meshes", "data", "bin", "build"
]

FILE_PREFIXES = [
    "mesh", "model", "tri", "quad", "cube", "sphere", "bunny", "armadillo", "teapot",
    "sample", "case", "scene", "geom", "iglfuzz"
]

FILE_SUFFIXES = [
    "", "_v1", "_v2", "_small", "_large", "_normals", "_tex", "_tri", "_quad", "_mix"
]

def _rand_token(r: random.Random, min_len: int = 3, max_len: int = 10) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(r.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(n))

def _maybe_unicode(r: random.Random) -> str:
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        return r.choice(UNICODE_FRAGMENTS)
    return _rand_token(r)

def _build_rel_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build 0-3 nested directories
    depth = r.randint(0, 3)
    parts: List[str] = []

    # Occasionally start with "." or ".." to ensure relative path behavior
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        parts.append(".")
    elif r.random() < 0.05:
        parts.append("..")

    for _ in range(depth):
        if r.random() < 0.6:
            parts.append(r.choice(DIR_NAMES))
        else:
            parts.append(_maybe_unicode(r))

    # Filename
    prefix = r.choice(FILE_PREFIXES) if r.random() < 0.8 else _maybe_unicode(r)
    suffix = r.choice(FILE_SUFFIXES)

    # Optional numeric infix for variety
    infix = ''
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        infix = f"_{r.randint(0, 9999)}"

    ext = r.choice(EXTS)
    fname = f"{prefix}{infix}{suffix}{ext}"

    parts.append(fname)

    # Join with OS separator, but ensure we do not create absolute paths
    path = os.path.join(*parts) if parts else fname

    # Ensure path length cap
    if len(path) > 200:
        path = path[-200:]
    return path

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose between a plain filename in current directory or nested relative path
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        # Simple filename variant
        prefix = r.choice(FILE_PREFIXES)
        if r.random() < 0.25:
            prefix = _maybe_unicode(r)
        num = r.randint(0, 1_000_000)
        ext = r.choice(EXTS)
        path = f"{prefix}_{num}{ext}"
    else:
        path = _build_rel_path(r)

    # Avoid path traversal that escapes too far; sanitize double separators
    path = path.replace('//', '/').replace('\\\\', '\\')

    # Ensure under size limits
    data = path.encode('utf-8')[:4096]
    return data
